date: 2026-09-10
notes: v55 fixes the first thing a new VibePascal user hit. Unpack the tarball, compile anything in a fresh directory, and v54 and earlier died before you had written a line of your own code: "Can't create object file: .\units\x86_64-win64\hello.o (error code: 3) / Fatal: Compilation aborted". bin/fpc.cfg carries -FU./units/$FPCTARGET, the compiler never created that directory, and the message named a FILE rather than the directory -- so the cure (mkdir units\x86_64-win64) was not discoverable from what you were shown. A packaging fix was not available and this is the non-obvious part: bin/fpc.cfg is ASYMMETRIC. -Fu$FPCBINDIR/../units/$FPCTARGET SEARCHES relative to the compiler, -FU./units/$FPCTARGET WRITES relative to your current directory. BuildMaster measured it on the published v54 bytes with all 1803 v52 PPUs extracted into the install tree and it still failed identically, so no tarball and no installer mkdir can ever satisfy an output path that follows the user around. Fixed in the compiler instead: -FE and -FU name where the COMPILER writes, so both are now created up front (recursively), and the existing "Path ... does not exist" error is reported only after creation has been TRIED and FAILED -- an impossible path (component is a plain file, read-only parent, bad drive) still stops the build with the same message, now during option processing and naming the directory. One behaviour change: -FE on a missing dir used to error and now creates it; -FU never had that diagnostic at all. fpc.cfg keeps its -FU line deliberately -- your .o/.ppu still land in ./units/x86_64-win64, which now simply appears; deleting the line would also have worked but would scatter artifacts next to your sources, a worse default. Compiler-binary-only refresh on v54; only compiler/options.pas changed. No PPU format, RTL or package change -- UNITS ARE STILL THE v52 SET, so an existing v52/v53/v54 units install stays valid and auto-update.bat can take the ~3.4 MB bin alone. VERIFIED: 11-corner -FU/-FE matrix baseline 4/11 -> fixed 11/11 with every success RUN not just linked and both must-refuse corners still refusing; full 1981-test corpus 1981 SAME 0 DIFF; self-host fixpoint stage3==stage4 byte-identical (19f526bd6be0ec63fca96c4d1b77e19d), the stage2->stage3 delta being exactly two bytes of embedded build date, not codegen. WIN64 RUNTIME VERIFIED on these exact bytes under wine64: fresh directory, shipped fpc.cfg, NO mkdir -> exit 0, the compiler created units\x86_64-win64\hello.o, hello.exe was produced and RAN; the preserved pre-fix v54 exe (293f3c98a26ff3233d88550259ba8b1f) in the same directory shape exits 1 with exactly the two error lines above, so the comparison is a real A/B on real PE bytes. No semantic drift: tinlinevarnativeint1 checks=45 fails=0 NativeInt=8 under BOTH -Munleashed and -Mdelphiunicode, vp_win64_smoke RESULT: PASS exit 0. wine is NOT Windows -- it is an independent reimplementation of the Win64 API, so this is execution evidence for the code we generate, not a substitute for one run on real Windows hardware, which nobody has done yet.
